modv0.1.2

climbRun a goal as a climb.

The mod runs your check after every turn, logs score and timing, protects named files, and queues the next iteration until the check passes or a stop condition fires.

At the prompt of a terminal session:

/plugin install climb --marketplace LeSplooch/tbaguette-skills
Other ways to install

  • From a shell:

    claude plugin install climb --marketplace LeSplooch/tbaguette-skills

  • In the desktop app: click + next to the prompt box, then Plugins, Add marketplace with LeSplooch/tbaguette-skills, then Add plugin.

Read designing-verifiable-goals Source on GitHub

How it works

Every iteration runs this loop. The check’s exit code is the only vote.

  1. 1The model’s turnThe model works toward passing, then ends its turn.
  2. 2The check runsThe mod runs your check itself. Its exit code counts; the model’s account of how it went does not.
  3. 3A row in the logExit code, score, check time and turn time, measured by the mod and the engine, not reported by the model.
  4. 4Bar met, or againExit 0 ends the climb. Anything else queues the next iteration, until a stop condition fires.

Commands

CommandWhat it does
/climb 20 npm teststart: up to 20 iterations, the check is npm test; the mod queues the first iteration itself
/climb 20 --in ../app make testrun the check in ../app; the log and protected paths live there too
/climb protect tests fixturesrefuse edits to these paths while it runs
/climb stall 5stop after 5 iterations with no better score
/climb ceiling 42end the climb at 42% of the weekly usage window; add 5h for the 5-hour one
/climb stopend it
/climbshow the climb and its last steps

What stops it

  • Bar met when the check exits 0. Anything else is another iteration.
  • Score, optional: the last score: <number> the check prints, higher is better. With scores, the climb also stops once it goes the stall limit without beating its best.
  • Stops on the bar, the budget, the stall limit, a spend ceiling, /climb stop, the Stop button, a turn you interrupt, or a check that runs past ten minutes or cannot start. Starting again is a fresh climb: the earlier one's history is discarded. An iteration prompt already queued when the climb stops is dropped.
  • Only its own prompts advance it. A prompt you send yourself mid-climb is answered normally and does not count as an iteration or run the check.

What it protects

Protected: Edit, Write, MultiEdit and NotebookEdit on a protected path, and on the log, are refused, matched by spelling and, for a file that exists, by its real path.

The limitA shell command is not inspected, so this limits the easy route rather than sealing the check; keep what the check reads somewhere the run cannot write if that matters.

The check runs with sh -c in the climb's folder, with a ten-minute timeout.

The log, from a real run

Log: .climb-log.tsv in the climb's folder (the session folder, or --in) holds the current climb, one row per iteration: exit code, score, check time and turn time, both measured by the mod and the engine rather than reported by the model. A climb whose turns are short and whose checks are long is waiting on the check, not short of ideas.
